comments.author: siliconc0w
comments.text:
I think it'd be interesting for a firm to try to run without traditional software.  Like the computer boots, you get a floating orb and you tell it stuff, it remembers, it stores it in an optimal format, it is capable of receiving, triaging, and sending synchronous or asynchronous communications externally or around the organization.  It knows how to build just-in-time tools and can recall any information, displaying it in the most helpful format.
It's not clear what 'work' those orbs would be doing because a lot of 'work' exists because of current frictions due to bad tools or some arbitrage around a lack of trust or expertise.  For example with contract redlines, if I just tell my AI what is important to me, and you tell yours, they can collaborate on a shared agreement that is essentially guaranteed to be fair (modulo trusting the AI).   No emailing word documents back and forth, no ambiguity of obligations, no hiding misleading terms, etc.

stories.title_en: ZeBridge – PostgreSQL replicas on devices, synchronized over NATS

comments.author: ndrean
comments.text:
I built ZeBridge to keep a local database on each device (SQLite, PGlite or DuckDB) in sync with a central PostgreSQL, for apps that must keep working on a bad connection.
It's aimed at B2B operational apps (fleets, depots, field teams), where each customer organisation is a tenant. It isn't built for consumer apps with one tenant per user.
How it works: a bridge written in Zig reads PostgreSQL's logical replication and publishes changes to NATS JetStream, one stream per tenant. Clients seed from snapshots kept in the NATS object store, then follow the stream. Writes made offline wait in a local outbox. When the device reconnects they go to PostgreSQL, which applies your rules (functions, row-level security) and sends back a verdict for each one. PostgreSQL stays the authority; NATS only carries the data.
The same NATS connection also reaches your own services. The live demo uses this to ask a routing service for a truck's route:
https://bridge.zebridge.eu/demo
(five trucks on a map of 16,173 charge points; open it in two tabs).
Clients: TypeScript (browser and Node), and a native Zig library with a C ABI, wrapped for Swift, Android, React Native, Flutter and Python.
